investigations.label: depth_1
investigations.text: The graph returned this evidence path: ACC-4471 → DEV-f31c → ACC-10477. Review the transfer evidence before deciding. These connections do not establish laundering; a named analyst must assess them.

unsupported_claims: The thesis path ACC-4471 -> DEV-f31c -> ACC-10477 shows only a shared device link, which is not evidence of laundering on its own
Pass-through or layering pattern is plausible (86.89M in, 66M out, ACC-10477 sent 11M and received 11M back) but is not established by structure alone
missing_queries: Other accounts using DEV-f31c and the timing/frequency of device sessions
Onward flows from ACC-3 (received 55M) and full ACC-10477 profile and history
Baseline for ACC-4471 to judge whether these in/out volumes are unusual for the account

investigations.label: depth_4
investigations.text: The graph returned this evidence path: ACC-4471 → DEV-f31c → ACC-10477 → DEV-r00-1 → ACC-1. Review the transfer evidence before deciding. These connections do not establish laundering; a named analyst must assess them.

unsupported_claims: The thesis only states that a graph path exists; the shared-device path (ACC-4471 → DEV-f31c → ACC-10477 → DEV-r00-1 → ACC-1) is supported structurally but does not itself show laundering.

The evidence shows many similar-sized inbound UPI transfers (~11M each) and a 55M outbound, but nothing establishes the intent or typology; the reading of them as a pattern is inference, not evidence.
missing_queries: Full transaction timeline for ACC-4471 including all outbound edges (66M out vs only 66M shown across two edges; in_sum 86.89M vs ~77M of inbound edges listed) to reconcile totals
Device DEV-f31c and DEV-r00-1 history: how many accounts share them, login timestamps, and whether sharing is benign (e.g. family or shared infrastructure)
Onward flow from ACC-3 and ACC-10477 to determine whether funds aggregate and exit

investigations.label: hold_proposal
investigations.text: The graph returned this evidence path: ACC-4471 → DEV-f31c → ACC-10477 → DEV-r00-1 → ACC-1. Review the transfer evidence before deciding. These connections do not establish laundering; a named analyst must assess them.

unsupported_claims: The thesis is a graph path (ACC-4471 → DEV-f31c → ACC-10477 → DEV-r00-1 → ACC-1) and says nothing about transfer behaviour; shared devices alone do not show money movement or laundering.

The profile shows six inbound transfers of ~11.0M-11.06M within about 5 minutes and 66M of outflow (55M of it to ACC-3), which suggests pass-through, but the thesis does not state this and the evidence does not confirm the funds moved onward as described.
Not all rows are verified: only a subset of edges is shown (TX-12, TX-8 outbound; TX-1 to TX-7 inbound), and in_sum of 86.89M does not reconcile with the visible inbound edges (~77.2M).
missing_queries: Full transaction history for ACC-4471 and linked accounts, with timing of in/out flows to test pass-through and structuring, and reconcile in_sum.
Device-sharing context for DEV-f31c and DEV-r00-1 (number of accounts per device, whether it is a common or shared-network device) to rule out benign overlap.
Account ages, KYC and expected-activity profiles for ACC-4471, ACC-10477 and ACC-1 to judge whether this volume is unusual.
